# yue-token-cost
**English** | 中文
**Measure what Chinese/Cantonese actually costs in tokens — and why.**
MCP server + DSH plugin. No GPU, no data, no model training: deterministic text measurement only.

> Status: **v0.1.0, published to npm.** `npx -y yue-token-cost` works today; 18 tests + 9 stdio
> sm

oke checks + a Node-vs-Python benchmark cross-check (48 rows) pass, and DSH's own MCP client
> spawn
s the published package and completes all three tools (4/4).
## Why
Same meaning, different scripts, very different bills. Measured over the 6-item HK labour/legal test
set in `BENCHMARK.md`:
| Tokenizer | English | 简体 | 繁體 | 粵語 |
Two things this makes visible, neither of which a plain token counter tells you:
1. **繁體/粵語 still cost 18–24% more than 简体** on modern tokenizers — and on the older one, Chinese as

a whole costs **+52% (简) to +79% (粤)** vs English.
2. **Switching tokenizer generation beats rewriti
ng your text**: the same 简体 text drops **128 → 83 tokens (−35%)** from `cl100k` to `o200k`.
Existing tools count one string with one tokenizer. They do not compare scripts, and they do not exp
lain *why* the extra tokens exist. This one does.

## Verified
Every claim here is checkable. What has actually been run, and how:
| Check | Command | What it proves |
| Unit + contract tests | `npm test` | 18 tests: attribution boundaries (half-character, digit split

ting, leading space), schema strictness, determinism |
| End-to-end over stdio | `npm run smoke` | 9
checks driving `server.mjs` with the official MCP client: tool list, strict-schema rejection, `stru

cturedContent` mirroring |
| Benchmark contract | `npm run bench` | 48 rows match the Python `tiktok

en` baseline row by row - Node and Python are two independent implementations |
| Vocabulary numbers
| `python bench/vocab_stats.py` | 200,019 / 105,898 / 7,532 - the figures the launch posts quote fo

r *why* the gap exists |
| DSH's own MCP client | `node scripts/dsh-e2e.mjs --target npm` (needs `DS
H_CHECKOUT`) | DSH's stdio transport factory spawns the server through `npx` and completes all three

tools (4/4) |
| Packed tarball | `npm pack`, then `dsh plugin add <tgz>` in an isolated `DSH_HOME`
| The published file set is complete: the bundle composes `mcp-client(serverName: yue-token-cost)` |
| The published package | `npx -y yue-token-cost --version` | Registry install works: exit 0, stdou
t empty, `0.1.0` on stderr |
CI runs the first four on every push (two jobs, Node 22).

Two npm details worth knowing: the registry also carries a `0.0.0-stage` entry — that is npm's
name-
reservation placeholder for staged publishing, not a failed release; `latest` points at `0.1.0`. A f

irst
publish of a new name goes through that staging flow and becomes live a few seconds later.
## Develop

Needs Node ≥ 22 to install with pnpm 11 (pnpm itself imports `node:sqlite`); the published
package d
eclares and supports Node ≥ 20 at runtime.

## Tools
| Tool | Input | Output |
| `count_tokens` | `text`, `tokenizer?`, `usd_per_million?` | tokens / chars / bytes, and cost if a

rate is given |
| `compare_scripts` | `texts[]` (same meaning, different scripts), `tokenizers[]?` |

side-by-side counts + delta + **attribution** |
| `explain_split` | `text`, `tokenizer?` | per-toke
n breakdown, flagging half-characters, digit splits, leading-space variants |

## Non-goals (v1)
No Jyutping (already covered by `tinci-mcp` — depend on `tojyutping` if needed), no dictionary, no A
SR, no model training, no web UI, no "auto-rewrite to save tokens".
## Benchmark
`BENCHMARK.md` is generated, not hand-written:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Every number in the README comes from that file. Scope and honesty notes (which tokenizers are cover
ed, why ratios are not universal constants, why identical 简体/繁體 items are kept) are at the bottom of
why ratios are not universal constants, why identical 简体/繁體 items are kept) are at the bottom of it.
Other tokenizer families are measured separately: `docs/deepseek-tokenizer.md` — the same testset on
DeepSeek V3/V4, and why V3→V4 does not change your per-token bill.
## Roadmap
- **v1** — 3 tools above, `o200k_base` + `cl100k_base`, npm + DSH bundle, tests, generated benchmark

.
- **v2** — local-model tokenizers as separate rows (`hf:<repo>`), glossary-aware "cheaper equivale

nt wording" suggestions.
- **v3** — optional `cantonese_asr` (local `whisper-small-cantonese`) — the
first thing here that needs a GPU.
